reward_resolution.how_the_validator_resolves_it: carried verbatim from the pattern document (the resolution path is unchanged): v2._configs_v2 hands environment.reward_profile to v2._reward_config_v2; each of profile_id, win_reward, failure_reward, time_penalty_per_native_tick present in the mapping OVERRIDES the v2 defaults; score_progress_reward_cap is owned by TrainerV2Config (trainer_v2.score_progress_reward_cap, here 1.0). profile_id is a label checked only for non-emptiness; the id win-time5x-score-truncation-neutral-v3 is REUSED because the profile it names is bitwise the same profile.
reward_resolution.ordering_guarantees: the composed training wrapper is DenseShapingObservableHumanSpeedrunWrapper; its _validate_reward_ordering enforces minimum win return > maximum terminated-failure return: (10 + (-0.0005 x 12000)) = +4.0 > (-10 + 1.0) = -9.0, satisfied with margin 13.0 at jungle6's max_ticks 12000 (identical arithmetic to the pattern: jungle levels are not in the long-horizon prefix list). The base-wrapper one-second dominance rule is deliberately dropped by the v2 dense-shaping mixin, exactly as documented in the pattern.
reward_resolution.magnitude_rationale: 5x clock signal, unchanged from the validated recipe. At the measured panel median (11991 ticks, hold 4, max_ticks 30000) the time term costs ~-6.0 against +10; at the training horizon the worst POSSIBLE win costs -6.0, still netting +4.0, so winning strictly dominates everything and the residual gradient on winning episodes is the clock. A 500-tick speedup is worth +0.25 per episode, the same well-posed polish signal that took Jungle1 from median 3833 to 3058.

hold_ticks_decision.training_source: ParkSettleActionConfig.hold_ticks default (src/zuma_rl/park_settle_action_wrapper.py); NO existing configuration path can set it for training (v2b's _make_env passes no park_settle_config; neither TrainerV2Config nor the CLI exposes a hold_ticks knob), and this campaign forbids editing frozen tools - so TRAINING RUNS AT hold_ticks 8, exactly as in the pattern document, and the asymmetry is preregistered rather than papered over.
hold_ticks_decision.evaluation_source: carried from the Jungle1 paired 2k-seed hold A/B (hold 4 ~90 ticks faster at the median, win rate within noise on identical seeds) and validated in practice by every timepolish checkpoint eval to date; ADDITIONALLY, this document's own init baseline was measured at hold 4 on the exact panel (lineage.init_baseline_panel16), so for THIS level the hold-4 evaluation of a hold-8-trained policy is directly receipted at init: 12/16 wins.
hold_ticks_decision.asymmetry_note: train at 8, evaluate at 4. HONEST CAVEAT: the A/B receipt is Jungle1 evidence; no jungle6 hold A/B exists. The init baseline receipts the hold-4 transfer for the INIT model only; if the hold-4 eval win rate collapses under training while telemetry stays healthy, that is a transfer failure and early_stop_rules clause (a) catches it - same guard, same clause, as preregistered in the pattern.

early_stop_rules.checkpoint_eval_protocol: 16-seed held-out panel, seeds 1494001000..1494001015, level Jungle3, hold_ticks 4, stack lags 0,4,8, deterministic masked predict, via tools/probe_alphazuma_55_macro_native_eval_v1.py (sha256:f36c6af8ebb481f21736f9a4fb79538463a27b69edb450b51d428193a290c23d) run ONE SEED PER INVOCATION at the probe's default max_ticks 30000 into eval16-ckpt<N>/seed-<seed> run dirs - the protocol is bit-for-bit the init-baseline protocol (lineage.init_baseline_panel16) and matches every eval16-* receipt already in this campaign; eval device chosen at eval time so as not to preempt training (this run holds cuda:1); metrics recorded: wins/16, median winning ticks over the wins, shots_on_target_rate

clause_a_win_rate_floor.quantization_rationale: one-seed-dip tolerance carried from the jungle8 rematch prereg: the 16-seed panel quantum is 6.25pp, so the margin is exactly one seed. From a 16/16 init, 15/16 passes; 14/16 or worse at two consecutive checkpoints stops the run.
clause_a_win_rate_floor.clause: if the 16-seed eval win rate is below 0.9325 (i.e. 14/16 or fewer wins) at TWO CONSECUTIVE checkpoints, STOP the run and keep the best earlier checkpoint
clause_a_win_rate_floor.best_checkpoint_rule: best = lowest expected time E[t] = median_winning_ticks / win_rate among checkpoints at-or-above the floor; the init (16/16, median 4660, E[t] 4660) is the fallback champion if no checkpoint beats its E[t]

clause_b_stagnation_success.clause: if the median winning ticks of the 16-seed eval fails to improve on the best median observed so far at THREE CONSECUTIVE checkpoint evals, CONCLUDE THE RUN SUCCESSFULLY with the best checkpoint
clause_b_stagnation_success.best_checkpoint_rule: best = lowest median winning ticks among checkpoints whose 16-seed win rate is >= the clause (a) floor (0.70)
clause_b_stagnation_success.rationale: time-polish saturates; three flat checkpoints (~786k steps) is the preregistered definition of converged. This clause is not a hypothesis: it fired on Jungle1 exactly as designed and banked the champion. UNCHANGED from the pattern document except that its best rule references the relative floor.

initial_model.space_check_note: macro-native by construction (distilled directly on macro decisions); v2's prevalidation passes it directly - no transplant step in this lineage. Adjudicated by the --validate-only launch gate.
initial_model.value_head_note: the BC trainer leaves the critic untrained; v2's fresh-start path copies the policy bitwise and starts a clean optimizer - first checkpoints may be critic-warm-up dominated (Jungle1 precedent), which the one-seed-dip floor tolerates

trainer_v2.reward_alignment: cap 1.0 and the 5x time term carried unchanged from the validated recipe. Arithmetic at jungle6's max_ticks 12000: worst win = 10 - 6.0 = +4.0; best truncation (truncation-neutral) = about -6.0 + 1.0 = -5.0; best terminated failure = -10 + 1.0 - time < -9.0. Ordering: every win > every truncation > every terminated failure; on winning episodes the clock is the dominant residual signal, which is the entire point of this run.
trainer_v2.discounting_note: gamma applies PER MACRO STEP; the macro reward is the undiscounted per-tick sum over the ticks the macro consumed, so 0.999 per macro is roughly 0.999^(1/40) per native tick; truncation is reward-neutral (v2 wrapper), so a timed-out episode bootstraps instead of paying -10
